requirements.title: Block execution begins with the first executable construct in the block
requirements.definition: Execution of a block begins by executing its first executable construct. Empty-block consequences are determined by the construct that contains the block and by its own execution rule.

requirements.oracle: Use final values from ordinary assignments, not call counts or side effects, to establish the beginning of nonempty block execution.

requirements.title: Block execution completes through last-construct completion, outward branch, RETURN, or containing EXIT/CYCLE
requirements.definition: Execution of a block is completed when the last executable construct completes without branching to a statement in the block, when a branch within the block has a target outside the block, when a RETURN statement in the block executes, or when an EXIT or CYCLE statement that belongs to a construct containing the block executes.

pending.last-construct-completion: PENDING positive-control source shape in which the final construct in a block assigns a distinct value and subsequent execution after the block observes it; no branch occurs to a statement inside the block.
pending.outward-branch-completion: PENDING positive-control source shape with an in-block branch to an outside target after 11.2 registration, verifying only reached outside control and leaving branch semantics to 11.2.
pending.return-completion-source: PENDING source-control plan for RETURN inside a block within a procedure after RETURN semantics are registered; no procedure call-count oracle is used.
pending.exit-cycle-containing-construct-completi: PENDING source-control plan for EXIT and CYCLE that belong to a containing construct, credited only after the corresponding constructs and statement ownership are registered.

requirements.oracle: This requirement enumerates completion causes; it does not define branch syntax, RETURN effects, EXIT/CYCLE ownership, or any statement execution count.

review_rationale: batch111: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). This batch opens Clause 11, so it establishes the shape later Clause 11 packets follow. The reviewer read all 44 base units of 11.1.1 Blocks, 11.1.2.1 Control flow in blocks, 11.1.2.2 Execution of a block, 11.1.3.1 through 11.1.3.4 the ASSOCIATE construct, and 11.1.4 the BLOCK construct in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verifying the titles from the source and confirming 44 base / 77 fine units, 42 requirements and 119 facets (all pending). The accounting claim was verified independently: the 20 numbered items R1101 in 11.1.1, R1102 through R1106 with C1101 through C1106 in 11.1.3.1, and R1107 through R1110 with C1107 through C1110 in 11.1.4 were already inventoried, so 24 non-numbered units are newly accounted, with no double count and no drop. Five permissions were adjudicated and accepted, including the 11.1.4 p3 explicit processor latitude for specification-expression evaluation order, which carries no plan asserting the processor took a particular order. Critically, the sentences of the form it is permissible to branch to an end statement only from within its construct do two things at once, permitting the inward branch and through the word only prohibiting the outward one, and the reviewer confirmed the packet captures both halves rather than losing a restriction or a permission. The attribution table was audited in full: all 30 negative rows were checked, including the R1109 row whose prohibiting words are a grammar production rather than a shall, the seven C1107 rows drawn from one prohibition list covering COMMON, EQUIVALENCE, INTENT, NAMELIST, OPTIONAL, statement functions and VALUE, the three C1101 rows and the four rows filed under 11.1.3.3 p5 that quote long compound sentences, confirming each negative isolates exactly one clause. The author's decision to treat C1104 as source-classification only was independently examined and accepted, because ordinary pointer assignment is conforming through the variable selector alternative, and 11.1.3.4's zero facets were accepted because its single note base unit and fine unit remain accounted. Decision: source-eligible, no blocking findings. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
